content.text: The document contains no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall, or volume-commitment language anywhere. Compensation is purely task-by-task time-and-materials, and either party may terminate for convenience on 15 days' notice.

input.quote: During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall penalty or volume restriction on Clear Capital, so it meets the preferred position rather than merely the fallback. Compensation under § 3(a) is time-and-materials as set out in each Statement of Work, and § 1(a) engages Contractor only "on a task by task basis," meaning Clear Capital pays solely for services it actually orders. There is no committed spend to reduce or true up, and § 6(a) additionally permits either party to terminate for any or no reason on fifteen (15) days' notice whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding, so no multi-year lock-in exists. A full-text search for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "retainer", "take or pay" and "volume" returned only unrelated hits (exclusive property/licence in § 4 and the entire-agreement clause in § 7). Noted for context only, and not a deviation under this rule: § 3(b) lets Contractor change rates on 30 days' notice, which is a pricing rather than a commitment issue and belongs to any price-increase rule. No redline required.
